existing_terminology:
“Sprachentwicklungsstörung (SES)”, abbreviated SES throughout (IS1406 survey translation)
For the primary form it gives the German-specific gloss “umschriebene” SES
Secondary SES is SES mit Komorbiditäten, co-occurring with other conditions
Translated by the joint German and Austrian team, Buchmann and Kauschke for Germany
existing_identificationCriteria:
The procedure for establishing special educational need differs from Land to Land
Parents, the school or other responsible services may apply to start it
School and school supervisory authority then decide, with parents involved
Evidence rests on a child-and-environment analysis of language competence
Interdisciplinary work may draw in ENT, phoniatrics, neurology and paediatrics
existing_assessments:
LITMUS sentence repetition (SRep) task for German
Developed by Cornelia Hamann and Lina Abed Ibrahim (Oldenburg), with Chilla and Ruigendijk
SRep reported highly sensitive and specific; LITMUS built for multilingual children
Extensively published — Hamann & Abed Ibrahim (2017), and on Arabic- and Turkish-German
Records that the instrument exists — not that any service here uses it
existing_multilingualProvision:
Practitioner perceptions, not policy — COST IS1406 survey 2017, n = 137 (Law et al., 2020)
Assessment: mainstream only 77%
Intervention: mainstream only 83%, two+ languages 10%
Interpreters sometimes used — assessment 59%, intervention 31%, counselling 74%
Access runs through a medical prescription (Scharff Rethfeldt, 2019, on Bremen)
existing_referralPathway:
Speech therapy on the sick funds requires a prescription by a contract doctor
Indication comes from overall functioning and context, not from the diagnosis alone
Treatment must begin within 28 calendar days of the prescription
Auditory processing disorder needs neuropsychological and central hearing diagnostics first
existing_serviceModel:
Practitioner-reported, COST IS1406 survey 2017, n = 258 from Germany (Law et al., 2020)
Settings: private practice 60%, nursery/kindergarten 28%
Sector: private 65%, public health 30%, public education 29%
Direct intervention most often weekly — 64%
Access shaped by: parental education 67%, social position 62%, urban/rural 61%
existing_legalEntitlement:
SGB V para 32 gives insured persons a claim to be supplied with Heilmittel
The G-BA directive binds the funds, the insured and contract doctors alike
Sick fund must decide an application within three weeks, five with an expert opinion
Missing the deadline without good reason means the benefit counts as approved
existing_funding:
One case per practitioner, more than one funder allowed — COST IS1406 2017, n = 258
Funders: health insurance 77%, state health 15%, state education 13%, state social services 9%
37% said a maximum number of sessions applied (n = 251)
existing_workforce:
Using the title Logopaede requires a licence under the Logopaedengesetz
Licence follows a three-year training and the state examination for logopaedists
Training is delivered at state-recognised schools for logopaedists
School support needs specialist-trained special-education teachers, KMK 1998
existing_outcomesEvidence:
KMK school statistics break out Förderschwerpunkt Sprache as a category of its own
Figures are asked of the Länder education ministries and compiled by the KMK secretariat
Sprache: 56,098 pupils in 2015 rising to 63,392 in 2024
KMK warns that in the worst case data on these Förderschwerpunkte can be lost
Published on a two-year cycle, this edition covering 2015 to 2024

existing_terminology:
No disorder category, service or school-language provision is named anywhere in it
Sourced absence, not an inference: 'speech' 0 in 147,617 chars of the cited report
Sanity check on the same text: 'Holy See' 136, 'Vatican' 15, 'school' 16
The report answers concluding observations on education, girls, health and the CRC
existing_identificationCriteria: Not established from the sources consulted. The Holy See's second periodic report to the Committee on the Rights of the Child records that children of Vatican City State attend legally recognised schools under various State legislation, and describes no school system inside the territory, so no body there identifies a language disorder.
existing_referralPathway:
Prescription from a doctor outside the fund needs approval by a DSI polyclinic doctor
Gynaecology, paediatric, eye, dental and dermatology visits need no prior authorisation
The prescribing doctor sets the priority band that governs access
If a deferrable service cannot be booked in 30 days an outside centre may be used
existing_serviceModel:
The DSI polyclinic's own service list has paediatrics and ENT but no logopedia
Therapy is bought in: FAS contracts named logopedia providers, all at Rome addresses
Each episode needs prior authorisation from a DSI or FAS-contracted doctor
Covers clergy, Vatican citizens and residents, and Holy See staff insured by the FAS fund
existing_legalEntitlement:
There is no national school system, so no support framework exists to record
The Holy See's own report to the UN says children attend schools elsewhere
The report names no health or education service inside the territory
Any entitlement therefore arises under the law of the State running the school
existing_funding:
The FAS health fund pays, via the DSI polyclinic or providers contracted to the fund
Indirect route: the family pays first and claims a pre-authorised reimbursement
Reimbursement uses the DSI tariff for anything its own polyclinic could have provided
The patient's share of the cost is paid at the counter before the service is given
Choosing an outside contracted provider over a DSI clinic leaves the tariff difference to pay
existing_workforce: Not established from the sources consulted. Neither the Direzione di Sanita e Igiene nor the Fondo Assistenza Sanitaria publishes any count of speech and language therapists. The FAS names six contracted logopedia providers by name, street address and telephone number, and the DSI's own list of services provided at its polyclinic runs from angiologia to medicina dei viaggi without naming logopedia.
existing_outcomesEvidence: Not established from the sources consulted for this entry — no school census or education statistic for Vatican City State was located, and the sources already on this entry are UN treaty documents and Holy See texts, which report on the Holy See’s international position rather than on any school population. If you work in this system, this is exactly the field to fill in.

existing_terminology:
The term is widespread in practice but not legally defined, and includes speech difficulties
Laws across entities and cantons use inconsistent terminology
existing_identificationCriteria:
No single state-level criteria: identification is set by entity and canton regulations
The enrolment procedure itself does not distinguish pupils with special needs
existing_referralPathway:
Categorisation is done by the centre for social work
Enrolment follows a professional team that includes speech therapists
First professional observation usually happens before primary enrolment
existing_serviceModel:
Preschool inclusion covers children with mild speech-voice communication disorders
Speech therapists sit on the school-entry team with pedagogues and psychologists
That centre performs the categorization and assessment of abilities
existing_legalEntitlement:
A framework law gives a right to education in regular schools
Provision is by a programme adapted to individual needs
existing_funding:
Schools educating these pupils receive earmarked budget funds
Funds cover the special programme, transport, accommodation and adaptation
existing_workforce:
In one entity's laws no right to a teaching assistant is established
In the other the question is not defined at all
Provision is uneven because lower levels of government differ
existing_outcomesEvidence:
In the Federation entity the ministry asked cantonal ministries by letter for the counts
A one-off Federal Ministry of Education and Science analysis, Mostar, October 2015
Tuzla canton returned 25 under Poremecaji u govoru, glasu i jeziku, of 306 categorised
The report doubts comparability: cantons do not use the same names for types of difficulty
One cantonal ministry puts the true number at two to two and a half times the recorded one

existing_terminology:
No language-disorder category was located in Andorran education law
The education Act speaks only of educational needs and pedagogical differentiation
The 2026 regulation is framed around pupils with disability, not disorder types
existing_identificationCriteria:
Conava must recognise the disability before specialised school support is assigned
A medical report and a parish social worker's valuation go with the application
The barems language chapter wants a diagnosis giving prognosis and skills preserved
Functional dislalia is not treated as a cause of permanent language disability
existing_referralPathway:
A centre needing more school-life accompaniment sends a justified demand to its inspector
At each year's end the inspector tells the centre next year's specialised staffing
The inspector issues a resolution within ten working days of receiving the demand
existing_serviceModel:
Organised from the educational environment, not tied exclusively to the individual pupil
Specialised support now runs on universal design principles
existing_legalEntitlement:
A new specialised-support regulation was approved on 8 July 2026
It replaces the model in force since 2008
The education Act obliges the government to run diversity plans
existing_funding:
Specialised materials come from the ministry through a loan service run by its areas
Centres themselves bear the cost of the ordinary materials their activity needs
The department maintains, repairs and replaces the material lent to the centre
existing_workforce:
A reference ratio of one specialised professional per five pupils with disability
A separate ratio of one school-life companion per five pupils
existing_outcomesEvidence: Not established from the sources consulted for this entry — the Govern d’Andorra education pages already on this entry carry no outcome reporting, and estadistica.ad serves its education tables only through a JavaScript portal that returned no readable text to this pipeline. If you work in this system, this is exactly the field to fill in.

existing_terminology:
The statutory category is children with special educational needs
A sub-category covers difficulties caused by linguistic and cultural obstacles
No separate statutory label for developmental language disorder was found
existing_identificationCriteria:
A professional team including parents prepares and adapts the programme
An individual development and education programme is due within 30 days of enrolment
It starts from an assessment of the child's present level and preserved potential
existing_referralPathway:
Wording is the consolidation to Sl. list 047/17; later changes are not in it
Usmjeravanje, the directing procedure, starts on a zahtjev, a request
Parent, primary health institution, school, social work centre or municipality may ask
The request is lodged with the competent local government body
A named commission proposes; the municipal education body does the directing
existing_serviceModel:
Mainstream inclusion is stated as the first option and an imperative
Resource centres deliver advisory work, teacher training and materials
Class size is cut by 10 per cent where such a pupil is enrolled
existing_legalEntitlement:
The basis is a 2025 Law on Education of Children with Special Educational Needs
Their education is defined as a public interest activity
existing_funding: Consolidation to 047/17: this education is financed from the budget of Montenegro
existing_workforce:
752 teaching assistants were engaged in 2025/2026
Speech therapists sit on the state mobile support teams alongside psychologists
existing_outcomesEvidence:
MONSTAT counts pupils with special educational needs by sex and by where they are taught
Its definition of that group names physical, mental and sensor difficulties, not speech
Drawn from the Ministry of Education Information System, at each school year's start
1,027 such pupils enrolled in 2020/21: 829 regular, 75 special, 123 in resource centres
No category of need is published, so children with language disorder are not visible
